header_summary:
The SHRINCS Working Group has introduced a draft of a new cryptographic Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP), which aims to implement a semi-stateful hash-based signature scheme, still in its prototype phase. This proposal, accessible at [SHRINCS.md](https://github.com/SHRINCS/shrincs-bip/blob/main/SHRINCS.md), is designed for compactness and speed but requires careful state management to avoid security risks. Significant contributions by Jonas Nick and Mikhail Kudinov have enhanced its compatibility and flexibility, addressing needs in high-frequency environments like the Lightning Network. The SHRINCS team is calling for community feedback to refine the design and ensure its security and effectiveness, with additional resources and discussions available, including a video at [this link](https://youtu.be/n-jGPICZMR0?si=NpfyTRB88-sUxtlh).

Recent updates to another Bitcoin Improvement Proposal have introduced clearer guidelines on locktime management to ensure effective enforcement and standardization across implementations. These changes, documented in the latest draft at [GitHub repository](https://github.com/nervana21/bips/blob/anti-fee-snipe/bip-anti-fee-sniping-with-locktime.md), include a new Rationale section that explains design decisions with links to relevant discussions ([Issue #26526](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26526) and [Issue #35628](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35628)). The updates aim to enhance privacy and consistency in transaction behavior, addressing community concerns and aligning with ongoing improvements within the Bitcoin ecosystem.

The discussion on consensus in blockchain technology emphasizes the economic implications of choosing and enforcing network rules, highlighting the distinction between operating full nodes and light clients. Full nodes are crucial for network security, preventing fraudulent activities, while light clients offer efficiency at the risk of reduced security unless configured correctly. Innovations like Utreexo are making it feasible to run full nodes with less resource intensity, as explored in resources available at [utreexod](https://github.com/utreexo/utreexod), [floresta](https://www.getfloresta.org/), and [optech](https://bitcoinops.org/en/topics/utreexo/). This evolution in technology encourages a pragmatic approach to consensus and security in the blockchain realm.

recent_posts.title: SHRINCS: an efficient hash-based signature scheme for Bitcoin (first draft)
recent_posts.summary:
- The SHRINCS Working Group has introduced a draft for a new cryptographic Bitcoin proposal.
- SHRINCS features include fast verification and post-quantum security with compact key sizes.
- The community is encouraged to review and improve the semi-stateful signing scheme's design.

recent_posts.summary:
- The BIP updates refine implementation details and clarify locktime management policies.

- New guidelines aim to document and standardize locktime policies for consistency.

recent_posts.title: Pragmatic definition of consensus for light clients
recent_posts.summary:
- Blockchain consensus revolves around enforcing rules and identifying the most work chain.
- Light clients rely on external validations, potentially posing operational risks.
- Innovations like Utreexo facilitate less resource-intensive node operations.

recent_posts.title: A design bar for coercion-resistant custody, and where duressfeatures land against it
recent_posts.summary: - The document compares jewelry theft and wrench attack statistics.  - Bitcoin self-custody costs exceed those of jewelry according to findings.  - Recommendations urge avoiding risky, opaque security practices for assets.

recent_posts.title: Covenants.diy: a node editor for covenant scripts
recent_posts.summary: - Recent programming opcode advancements offer a flexible framework for developers.  - Current opcodes like `OP_CHECKTEMPLATEVERIFY` and `OP_CAT` aid in application security.  - Further opcode developments like `OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY` will enhance protocol utility.

active_posts.title: Add importprivkeys RPC
active_posts.summary:
- Importing private keys into Bitcoin Core wallets is complex and widely discussed.
- A Python tool on GitHub now aids users in migrating private keys to descriptor wallets.
- A new 'importprivkeys' RPC call is proposed to streamline these imports further.

active_posts.title: post-quantum: solution ideas to "tripwire"game-theory issues + a certificate-based rescue protocol
active_posts.summary:
- Exploring blockchain solutions for "tripwire" issues is crucial against quantum threats.
- Alternatives include a new UTXO model and group signatures from upgraded coins.
- Technical measures involve using Bitcoin's blockchain for timestamped ownership proofs.

active_posts.title: DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol
active_posts.summary:
- DropKick aids Bitcoin users to securely transition to Post-Quantum wallets using blockchain commitments.
- It utilizes cryptographic proofs to allow spending old coins without prior PQ-safe UTXOs, minimizing blockchain impact.
- Unlike competing protocols, DropKick offers simpler implementation and uses third-party aggregators, enhancing flexibility.

active_posts.title: PQC output type discussion
active_posts.summary:
- The email explores strategies to protect Bitcoin from quantum threats using PQC and ECC.
- It suggests implementing a P2TRv2 output type for immediate quantum readiness and minimal disruption.
- Long-term strategies and ECC disabling timing are debated to ensure gradual adoption and security.

active_posts.title: Segwit commitment to post-quantum witness data?
active_posts.summary:
- Enhancing blockchain for post-quantum cryptography requires modifications like increased block sizes.
- Implementing these changes needs updates like new transaction identifiers and network adjustments.
- An alternative involves integrating post-quantum data within existing segwit areas to maintain efficiency.

active_posts.title: PQ-single-address-backup - BIP-38 for P2MR (bc1z) - 104-char encrypted backup format
active_posts.summary: - The PQ-SAB proposal enhances seed security with encrypted paper backups.  - Key derivation and encryption use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM.  - Community feedback and potential standardization discussions are ongoing.

today_in_history_posts.title: Statechain coinswap: assigning blame for failure in a two-stage transfer protocol.
today_in_history_posts.summary:

- The conductor manages statecoin swaps without learning owners’ identities, using blind signature schemes.
- Address assignment issues in the protocol could lead to failed transfers, with solutions under exploration.

today_in_history_posts.title: Witness asymmetric payment channels
today_in_history_posts.summary:
